name: Bill Lipschutz
caution_flags: early_personal_account_blowup_late_1970s: self-recounted in The New Market Wizards — grew a USD 12,000 inheritance to roughly USD 250,000 over several years, then lost essentially all of it within days on a single concentrated options position before his professional career began

name: Gary Bielfeldt
caution_flags: regulatory_action_cftc_position_limits_corn_1993: CFTC complaint (1995) alleging he exceeded speculative position limits in corn futures Oct-Nov 1993, including by controlling trading in his wife's accounts; an ALJ found him liable and Commission proceedings ran through a 2004 opinion and order (sources 1-2)

name: Paul Tudor Jones
caution_flags: sec_short_sale_settlement_1996: Tudor entities paid ~$800,000 (reported as the second-largest SEC fine in a non-fraud case at the time) over March 1994 short sales of Dow stocks that violated the uptick/short-sale rule; settled without admitting or denying the allegations (SEC Lit. Rel. 15038; Washington Post 1996).

name: Richard Dennis
caution_flags: managed_fund_losses_1987_88: clients in his managed pools suffered heavy losses (reported ~$50M total 1987-88, including ~$10M on Black Monday); he withdrew from managing client money in spring 1988 (Wikipedia).|investor_complaints_settled_1990: his firm settled investor complaints alleging failure to follow his own trading rules for over $2.5M, without admitting or denying wrongdoing (Wikipedia).|second_retirement_2000: returned to fund management in the 1990s (Dennis Trading Group) and reportedly stopped again around 2000 after drawdowns - reported in press/aggregators; exact figures not verifiable, so no numeric claim recorded.

name: Harry Markowitz
caution_flags: primarily_academic: no verifiable personal trading track record exists; profile value is theoretical lineage (mean-variance portfolio selection) plus the documented gap between his theory and his own regret-minimizing behavior.

name: John Meriwether
caution_flags: ltcm_1998_collapse: lost $4.6B in <4 months on ~25:1+ leverage; required a $3.6B Fed-coordinated private-consortium bailout (Sept 1998); systemic-risk case study (PWG report 1999).|jwm_2009_closure: post-LTCM firm JWM Associates shut its main Relative Value Opportunity II fund in July 2009 after a 44% loss (Sept 2007-Feb 2009) — the same style failed twice under stress.|salomon_1991_context: Meriwether resigned as Salomon vice-chairman amid the 1991 Treasury auction bid-rigging scandal involving a trader he supervised (paid a civil fine, was not charged with wrongdoing himself).

name: Victor Haghani
caution_flags: ltcm_1998_collapse_founding_partner: Haghani was a founding partner and one of LTCM's two biggest risk-takers; the fund lost $4.6B in 1998 and required a Fed-coordinated private bailout (Lowenstein; Federal Reserve History). He lost the bulk of his own fortune in the fund.
